items.title: 52115_Danny Barker oral history interview
items.q: Do you want to go with me to the Nest Club? I've got a job.

ctx.x: And they called him Father White, didn't they.
Yeah, Father White. So he came to me and said, 'Are you working?' I said, 'No.' He said, 'Do you want to go with me to the Nest Club? I've got a job.' I said, 'Yeah.' He said, 'Okay.'

So I started two weeks after I got to New York with Harry White in the Nest Club. A six-piece band. We go to work at ten o'clock. You might tune up until eleven, or fool around, because it was somewhat of an after-hour joint. It was a famous...

items.title: Danny Barker — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

ctx.x: How did you first get in Cab’s band?

I’m around there, and I’m starting from the bottom. It’s 1930, with Harry White’s band. I’m with Dave Nelson’s band. I’m with Danny Logan’s band. I’m with Luis Russell’s band. Played with Louis . . . played a short tour with Louis Armstrong, through Virginia. Bill Johnson got drunk, and Luis Russell wanted to hire somebody else. Paul told him, “If you hire somebody else, I quit. Hire my nephew.” So he hired me. Bill Johnson got well again and then Bill Johnson got drunk again. They had to tolerate Bill. Bill…
This is not the same Bill Johnson that played with King Oliver.
